records.locator: CP1252 lines2305–2321; original Sanskrit BPHS Chapter26 verses2–9, particularly 26.6–9
records.source_paraphrase: The translation first distinguishes planetary from sign aspects, then gives exact (sphuta) aspect strength through a piecewise oriented planetary longitude separation. Positive general aspect strength starts only beyond one 30° sign (verse26.9); the gap from 300° around zero to 30° has no ordinary positive aspect in the standard full formulation.
records.source_layer: Portuguese English-mediated BPHS with external Sanskrit 26.6–9 crosscheck (VedicPupil transcription), plus English published speculum; not independent critical manuscript edition
qualifications: This is GENERAL graha aspect strength, not special Mars/Jupiter/Saturn aspects or final Shadbala/Drigbala sum.

Mercury stays less than 30° in ecliptic longitude from Sun under a deliberately conservative physical bound (<29°). It therefore receives zero ordinary Sun aspect according to this formula in either directed elongation.
No human trait/outcome evidence; no production formula promoted.

records.locator: Sanjay Rath Lesson13, original Sutra1.1.2 and explicit commentary, uploaded PDF257–260
records.source_paraphrase: The printed short Jaimini 1.1.2 refers to facing and flanking signs; Rath's detailed commentary operationalizes movable signs aspecting fixed signs except their adjacent fixed sign, fixed signs aspecting nonadjacent movable signs, and dual signs aspecting other dual signs. Same/adjacent sign pairs do not aspect in this school version.
records.source_layer: Jaimini Sanskrit 1.1.2 PLUS separate school-specific Rath interpretation, not verbatim original sutra for all enumeration conditions
qualifications: Rasi drsti is sign-sign aspect and is not identical to BPHS continuous-degree graha drsti or Saravali ordinary planetary aspect.
Sun and Mercury remain in one sign or adjacent signs under conservative <29° separation, so none of these Rasi-drsti pairings applies to their signs.
Other Jaimini interpretations may differ; no human outcomes used.
